recipes.name: Judy’s Strawberry Pretzel Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Gather ingredients, and preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix together pretzels, melted butter, and 4 1/2 tablespoons sugar in a medium bowl until well combined. Press into the bottom of a 9x13-inch dish.
Press into the bottom of a 9x13 inch pan. Bake for 10 minutes, or until lightly toasted. Set aside to cool completely.
In a medium bowl, beat the sugar and cream cheese until smooth.
Fold in whipped topping and spread evenly over the cooled crust. Refrigerate until set, about 30 minutes.
Stir together boiling water and gelatin mix in a second large bowl. Mix in frozen strawberries; stir until thawed.
Pour over cream cheese mixture in the dish. Refrigerate until completely chilled, at least 1 hour.
Refrigerate until completely chilled, at least 1 hour. Slice and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Judy’s Strawberry Pretzel Salad
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry pretzel dessert salad features layers of salty, crunchy crust, sweet cream cheese, and Jell-O for a gorgeous, chilled dish everyone loves.

video.description: Looking for crowd-pleasing potluck dishes that are guaranteed to disappear fast? In this video, Nicole shares five fun and flavorful salad recipes that are perfect for barbecues, picnics, parties, or any group gathering. From creamy classics to sweet surprises, these salads are easy to make and impossible to resist. Nicole walks you through step-by-step recipes including bold and crunchy Fritos Corn Salad, nostalgic Strawberry Pretzel Salad, ultra-comforting Deviled Egg Macaroni Salad, sweet-and-creamy Cookie Salad, and a fresh, savory Celery and Parmesan Salad. These potluck favorites come together with simple ingredients and deliver big flavor with every bite.

review.reviewBody: This is always a hit! Tips I live by to make this turn out every time. 1) DON'T bake the pretzel layer any longer than 10 minutes. 2) Double the amount of jello to make it proportional to the amount of cream cheese. 3) Let the jello chill to thicken slightly before spreading on the cream cheese layer.

I have made this a few times now with perfect results. I read the reviews prior to making it and found it extremely helpful to do the following: 1) instead of using 2 cups of water, use 1 cup of boiling water to dissolve the package of gelatin, then add 3/4 cup strawberry juice/syrup, and then add the strawberries; and 2)put the gelatin/strawberry mixture in the fridge for about an hour or so to thicken a bit before pouring it overtop of the cream cheese mixture (this is very key for the success of the dessert). I really think these changes helped to enhance the texture and flavor of the gelatin layer. I highly recommend trying this. I have taken it to two dinner parties now and cannot tell you how many compliments I received, my friends were thoroughly impressed. Thanks for the fantastic recipe!!!

I have been making this for at least 15 years and everyone fights over it. They want to get their share. My recipe differs a little. It calls for 2 cups pretzels, marg. instead of butter and 3 tsp.( I use heaping tsps.) sug. for crust. For cheese middle it is the same only it calls for 1- 8 oz cream cheese instead of 2. Top layer is 2 small pkgs. jello,water the same,but use 2-10 oz. cartons frozen strawberries. I like Birdseye brand in syrup. If berries are whole, I chop them up. It really needs to chill several hours. This is my most requested jello recipe ever! It really is like a dessert! When I first made it, no one could figure out what the bottom was made of! You really must try. Thanks Tom!

I've made this several times for work potlucks. I would make it the night before and it always turned out beautifully (it's a big hit!). Once I made it during an afternoon for dinner that night and the pretzel crust was much too hard. I think the trick is letting it sit overnight long enough for the crust to soften. It's definitely my favorite!

Enjoyed by all. I used butter flavor pretzels. No one guessed it was a pretzel layer. I used fresh strawberries and made the jello as I was beginning the recipe. I then refrigerated and, by the time it came to do the jello layer, the jello had thickened enough for the strawberries to be folded in. Thanks for sharing!

The flavor of this salad is very tasty and universally loved. I just have a couple of tips for preparing. First, make sure you add non-stick spray to any vessel other than a non-stick pan. I used a glass pan, thinking the butter in the pretzel crust was enough to release from the pan. That totally wasn't the case. Second, make sure your pan is not only a 13x9 but is deeper than 1 3/4". I found this out the hard way when adding my strawberry jello layer and flooded the edges. I look forward to making this salad again with these couple of tweaks. Enjoy!

Love this recipe and have made several times. I use sugar free Jello and Sugar free whipped cream BUT do add the sugar mentioned in the recipe. Ive used a mix of fresh and frozen strawberries, even added a few ice cubes to help cool down the mix. As long as you stay below the 4 cup amount of liquid that the regular jello mix would have you add, youre fine. I did count the frozen berries toward this. Ive made it before with all fresh berries and no adtl liquid and that top layer is too solid. Also..we have a friend that has to eat gluten free. Found gluten free pretzels to use for the base. Worked just fine. Have also used low fat cream cheese in it, works fine too. A very forgiving recipe!

Excellent recipe. I used just 4 tablespoons of sugar in the crust. I also used low-far cream cheese and zero sugar Jello to cut a few more calories. I used frozen sliced strawberries (thawed) to cool the jello, but removed the berries and used about double the amount stated to completely cover the top. Then poured the jello over the strawberries. It worked great and my family loved having more strawberries! Also, I think next time I make it, I will use 3 cups of crushed pretzels for the crust as I had a hard time getting good coverage on the bottom of my pan.

I made this and I definitely recommend using fresh strawberries instead of frozen, the frozen strawberries were mushy and gross. The pretzels were also mushy even after baking for 15 minutes. So I will make again but I will use a pre made pie crust and fresh strawberries.

This is a very good recipe. I did make a few changes after reading several other recipes on line, and the fact that I bought fresh strawberries instead of frozen as called for. After seeing the total amount of crushed pretzel would not cover the pan, I went to 2 1/2 cup of crushed pretzel, and 8 tablespoons of butter. I let the jello cool off then I placed the sliced fresh strawberries on top of the cream cheese in a nice display, then slowly poured the jello over the strawberries.

I’ve made this for years changing the fruit/jello combination with seasonal offerings! This year for Thanksgiving I used a can of Ocean Spray “whole cranberry” cranberry sauce. I took the fruit out of the can & froze it while making the rest of the dessert. I split it into 2 deep dish pie plates. One for a family get together & one for Thanksgiving Dinner. Redoing for Christmas. DELISH!!

This is one of my family’s favorite dishes. The only substitution I make it washing and cutting up real strawberries and freezing them the night before. Then when I make the gelatin mixture, I add the frozen strawberry pieces with a ladle to cover the dish and then fill in the rest with the remaining gelatin. Perfect everytime.
Tasty and easy to make. BUT crust stuck to the bottom of the dish. Followed all directions. Would lining the dish with parchment paper make this keep everything intact?.
No changes to the recipe. It's perfect the way it is. Thank you for the recipe!
I've made this several times. My family and I absolutely LOVE it.
I've made this for many different occasions. My kids usually prefer this for their "birthday cake". So good with the salty sweet creamy vibe.
This recipe is a keeper and will be made often. The only change I really made was to make them in a cupcake liner instead of the cake pan.
My family requests this for large get-togethers Always a hit. I absolutely love it! I use gluten free pretzels because they stay crunchier longer!!
I've made this recipe many times and it's always been a crowd fav.
This is a holiday must have!
